newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Quickco attracts surge of market interest.
newsitem.headline: Quickco attracts surge of market interest.

text.p: A surge of market interest in South African transportation firm Quick Holdings Ltd (Quickco) propelled the stock higher on Thursday and saw volumes hit more than 20 million shares, dealer said.
At 1120 GMT the firm had jumped two cents to five cents as 20.58 million shares changed hands. It had earlier touched a new year high of six cents.
The flurry of trade was sparked by comments Quickco made to shareholders at its annual general meeting in Durban on Wednesday.
A Quickco spokesman told Reuters the firm had returned to profitability after three tough years and completed a restructuring programme that involved selling off loss-making units.

"We have restored the group to profitability and we feel that we can repeat the six month profit to December 31 in the next six months. We believe we can maintain our level of profitabilty. We could even do better, but we are comfortable with saying we can maintain it," the spokesman said.
The firm posted half year earnings per share to December 31, 1996, of 0.21 cents, up from a loss of 1.58 cents for the 18 months to June 30, 1996.
The firm is also on the hunt for possible buys. "We are poised to look at acquisitions," the spokesman added.
Dealers said trade was so heavy due to the firm's "penny share" status meaning traders were quickly getting in and out of the stock to capitalise on single cent rises in the price.
"You make your whole profit on that one cent so lots of guys are getting in and out in big volumes," one dealer said.
